newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine delays renouncing Soviet asset claims.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine delays renouncing Soviet asset claims.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament delayed ratification on Wednesday of a deal with Russia under which Kiev would renounce claims to Soviet assets in return for Moscow assuming Ukraine's share of Soviet foreign debt.

Deputies voted 233 to 70 to present Russia with a long list of conditions for ratification, including full information on money held by the Soviet central banking system when the Soviet Union broke up in 1991.
Ukrainian deputies also instructed the government to make deals with Russia to obtain what they said was Ukraine's share of gold and diamonds held by Soviet authorities, or a cash substitute.

In December 1994, then-Ukrainian Prime Minister Vitaly Masol and his Russian counterpart Viktor Chernomyrdin signed a "zero option deal" under which Kiev agreed to renounce claims to Soviet assets in exchange for Russia taking on all Soviet debts.
But Ukraine's conservative-dominated parliament has to approve the deal before it can come into force.
Russia has signed and ratified bilateral Soviet asset deals with all former Soviet republics except Ukraine.

Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the economy, Viktor Pynzenyk, told reporters after the vote: "This was a sensible compromise. Ukraine has not thrown out the principle of the zero option. They have told the government to hold talks to clear up several issues."
He said Ukraine had to find a compromise with Russia over the issue, which has been a thorn in the side of relations between the two countries since Kiev won independence in 1991.
